posts.name: Emethriel
posts.cooked:
Hey fellow World of Warcraft players,

I hope you’re all doing well and enjoying your adventures in Azeroth. I wanted to take a moment to discuss an issue that has been on my mind for a while now - the current state of Arcane Mages in the game. I believe it’s time for Blizzard to consider some changes and buffs to this spec to make it more competitive and enjoyable to play.

Arcane Mages have always been known for their unique playstyle and burst potential, but it feels like they have fallen behind in recent patches. Here are a few reasons why I think Arcane Mages deserve some attention:

  1. Mana Management: One of the defining characteristics of Arcane Mages is their use of mana as a resource. However, it can be extremely challenging to manage mana effectively in high-intensity situations like raids and dungeons. An adjustment to mana management mechanics could make the spec more accessible and engaging.
  2. Damage Output: Arcane Mages often struggle to keep up with other DPS classes in terms of sustained damage output. While their burst damage is impressive, it comes at a cost of a significant cooldown, leaving them less competitive during the rest of the fight. Some tweaks to their sustained damage could balance this out.
  3. Utility: Arcane Mages lack the utility and survivability options that other mage specs (Frost and Fire) possess. Adding some unique utility or survivability tools to the Arcane toolkit could make them more versatile in various situations.
  4. Talent Diversity: Some talents in the Arcane tree are rarely chosen because they simply don’t compare to others. By improving the viability of less-used talents, you could encourage more diverse playstyles within the spec.

I understand that balancing classes and specs in a game as complex as World of Warcraft is a difficult task, and I appreciate the effort Blizzard puts into maintaining balance. However, I believe that addressing some of the concerns of the Arcane Mage community could enhance the overall gaming experience for both dedicated Arcane players and the WoW player base as a whole.

I’d love to hear your thoughts on this matter and encourage everyone who shares similar sentiments to voice their opinions as well. Together, we can help make World of Warcraft an even more enjoyable and balanced game for everyone.

Thank you for your attention, and may your loot be epic!

Best regards, [Your In-Game Name] [Server Name]

posts.name: Archmage
posts.cooked: All true, except it’s all still very much relevant because even though DF undoubtedly improved upon many of these areas they’re all still major problems (perhaps with the exception of mana management which has been significantly trivialized but is never the less still a factor). To paraphrase Al Gore, it’s important to note that we’ve made progress but the world is still very much on fire.

posts.name: Desolation
posts.cooked:
Are there issues to be addressed? Sure. But this ChatGPT response is either backwards or so generic you could post it about almost any spec.

  1. Mana management is the opposite of what ChatGPT infers. It claims management is difficult, but you yourself said it’s trivialized now.
  2. Our sustained damage was improved a decent amount by the removal of RoP, however, arcane’s massive burst output is kinda the point of the spec at this point. Tweaking our sustained damage would come at the cost of reducing our burst, and would also lessen the impact that we can actually bring to an encounter.
  3. Utility is the only thing mentioned in this post that I find truly relevant. Arcane’s spec-specific utilities were given to the entire class as a whole with no compensation. Mages as a whole have, in my opinion, more utility than they did previously - especially with Mass Barrier - but arcane could use something specific to just them to help balance them out compared to frost and fire.
  4. Talent Diversity is something I’ve heard just about every class and every spec complain about. You could slap that onto a post about any spec and just change the word “Arcane” to the spec in question and I doubt people will disagree.

posts.name: Archmage
posts.cooked:
Right, they’re all still problems just to a lesser extend or in different ways. Mana management is now just an annoyance rather than a proper mechanic. Sustain is in an okayish state atm but a lot of that is tied to the current set bonus and burst took a hit after the removal of RoP with nothing to fill that void (again aside from the current set bonus). Utility is the biggest pain point. Mass Barrier is nice to have but a rather boring ability and is class wide, Arcane continues to have nothing to offer in the utility department unlike both Frost and especially Fire. And, yes, talent diversity is not just an Arcane problem it’s universal.

Just to clarify, I am content with the way the spec plays now, especially when it comes to AoE, and it’s generally markedly better than before but ST still needs a lot of work in addition to all the aforementioned areas.
